title: Functions II
subtitle: Spells You Can Hand Over
heading: ## Unit 7 ·

parts.scope: Lesson 6B "Recipes That Read Stat Sheets" (with 6B-remembers; all its exercises in order, including its solo)
Lesson 6C "Spells You Can Hand Over" (with 6C-remembers; all its exercises in order, including its solo), Quiz 6B, and Project 6P "The Resonance Array" (with its side quest)

Extra practice 7X (6B-08 default and keyword arguments, 6B-09 scope), the optional Articles 6-A1 lambda, 6-A2 map() and 6-A3 "Two Things Back", Quick Check Recipes II (both forms as testout items, plus their question forms as optional quiz items, the way Units 1-5 did) and the Spell Recipes cheatsheet

slips: a function that changes a dict passed in vs one that must return a value (returning nothing, so the caller gets None; or thinking the caller won't see the change); building a dict whose keys don't exactly match the names the campaign reads ("magic" vs "magical_affinity", approximate names); quoting a parameter inside the dict ({"name": "name"}) instead of using it; typing literal test values instead of the parameters (still the class's biggest slip); an early return placed after the work, or a guard written as if/else that never returns; calling a helper with the wrong number or order of values, or editing a helper they were told to leave alone; passing a function WITH () (strengthen_magic() calls it now and hands over None; TypeError 'NoneType' object is not callable) instead of without; reading book[name]["effect"] without (hero) so nothing happens; storing the result of a call where the function itself was wanted; print inside the function instead of return; reading a key from the wrong sheet (caster vs target).
earlierNote: Units 1-2 are shipped (in this folder). Units 3 (Functions I), 4 (Lists) and 5 (Dictionaries) are verified in staging and copied into this folder. Unit 6 (Loops) is being written AT THE SAME TIME in another staging dir and is NOT in this folder; its concepts come from concept_map.json (prefixes u06a, u06b, u06c). Unit 7 may use loops ONLY within those planned concepts (for over a list or a list of dicts, while, break). Terminology from here on: "function" (Mar'tu still says "recipe"). Use the real party-table values.
verifyNote: Fix every Unit 7 error until 0 errors; with concept_map.json moved aside the u06 concepts are missing, so for errors that are ONLY 'concept not introduced yet' for tokens the plan gives to u06a/u06b/u06c, restore the map and re-run with it instead, and report those tokens (they get cross-checked when Unit 6 ships).
extra: Campaign callbacks: mana-bars (get_mana_bar, show_mana; Obj 1 and 6: build the bar, then pass it on), spell-book (add_spell; Obj 3, exact matching names), the opening of hold-the-barrier (Obj 4, early return), print_mana and reinforce_barrier (Obj 5, read a helper you didn't write and leave it unchanged), strengthen_magic without () and spell["spell_function"](caster) (Obj 7, a function as a value). Mar'tu's framing: "a recipe can sit in a box, like any value. You can hand it to someone without cooking it." CONVENTIONS from the Unit 2 walkthrough fixes (read the repo's FORMAT.md): "Start like this" hints go LAST, never hint 1, and the last hint's line must be in the solution (the harness warns on both — leave none); solo items and Quick Check builders use explainer="lean"; Quick Check check messages name the slip and the evidence but never the fix; Quick Check forms set questions_to_pass like Unit 2's QC2. Never use worksheet-derived names or "Tester" in check data; invented Tor names only.
